statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail has fallen back below the block threshold after an observed and so far holding retracement off the session low.
recommendation: Tail at 21 is in the 20-24 band, so the mapped state is WATCH, down from BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES an hour ago. The 19:00Z-20:30Z power-hour and cash-close window remains the narrow danger window. Existing-position management and protective logic are unaffected by this state.
headline: An observed bounce off the session low unwinds the failed-retracement structure, returning Tail to the watch band while high Stress persists
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index trades at 30,754.05, down 406.02 points or 1.30%, within a 30,556.40 to 31,125.13 session range against a 31,160.08 previous close. Nasdaq-100 December futures, the preferred continuous reference, are at 30,985.50, down about 1.33%, roughly 193 points above their 30,792.00 session low; a second independent feed corroborates both the level and the low. The decisive change from the prior hour is the price path rather than the level. At 13:16 to 13:26 ET the index was printing 30,580.58, down 1.86%, at a new session low with no recovery visible, which is why the previous assessment scored an observed failed retracement and extension at the extreme. The 14:26 to 14:27 ET quotes show the index about 198 points above that low and holding there, which is an actual retracement rather than a shallow pullback inside continued extension. Semiconductors confirm the same shift: the PHLX Semiconductor Index is at 12,701.31, down 364.84 points or 2.79%, about 217 points and 1.7% above its 12,483.95 session low, having been down 4.41% and pinned at its low an hour earlier. The macro amplifier stack has also continued to unwind while this bounce developed. The ten-year Treasury yield is 5.24, down about four basis points on the day and roughly nine basis points below its 5.33 session high, after reaching a 24-year high of 5.356 on October 7. The 17:00Z sale of 22 billion dollars of 30-year bonds came at a 5.618 percent high yield with a 2.54 bid-to-cover above the 2.41 average and only a 0.1 basis point tail, a solid result that removed the auction as a forward risk. The VIX is 15.88, up 5.31 percent but below 16 and off its own 16.46 session high, which is not the volatility structure that accompanies a pathological one-way path. Oil is the single amplifier still aligned with downside equity risk: WTI is near 91.72, up 3.90 percent, and Brent is near 104.31, up about 4.1 percent, after reporting that the Pentagon has told Central Command to finish preparing for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran and that President Trump has ruled out a deal, alongside fresh tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz. The driver mix today is therefore genuinely two-sided: a chip-specific repricing after Samsung's preliminary third-quarter results disappointed, which cooled the memory trade, plus an energy and inflation-expectations shock, set against easing long-end yields, a contained VIX and a successful long-bond auction. Under this provider's risk definition Tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion, not the size of the move or the importance of the catalyst. One of the two conditions that lifted Tail into the block band, persistent structure at the extreme, has been observed to fail, and multiple independent amplifiers are no longer aligned. Tail is therefore published at 21 in the watch band. Stress remains high at 67 because a second consecutive lower session, a 2.79 percent semiconductor decline, oil up four percent, hawkish Federal Reserve commentary from Governor Waller and an unresolved war with live headline-gap potential all describe a difficult environment that can still mean-revert. Confidence is 88: current index, futures, semiconductor, volatility and yield levels were each verified with explicit as-of timestamps, the long-bond auction result and the day's macro releases were confirmed against the published calendar, and the material news items were read at source. The shared Finviz context file was read as required but its collection timestamp is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with partial status and unavailable futures and calendar sections, so it was treated as stale and excluded from this assessment rather than allowed to stand in for live evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours began with a quiet mean-reverting overnight tape in which Tail decayed from 15 at 18:00Z to a low of 10 at 03:00Z while Stress held a 47 to 53 range. From 06:00Z the oil and long-end-yield impulse took over: Tail stepped to 22 at 07:00Z and then held a 20 to 23 watch-band range through the European and early US session, with Stress climbing from 55 to a 60 to 66 plateau. The 14:00Z slot eased to 17 as the US cash open proved orderly, before 15:00Z and 16:00Z returned to 20 and 22. The single block-band hour in the window is 17:00Z at Tail 28 and Stress 72, published on an observed failed retracement and extension to the session low. Dominant mode was mixed apart from trend-down readings at 06:00Z, 07:00Z, 11:00Z and 17:00Z. No published hour is rewritten here.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the watch band for the remainder of the US cash session, at 21 now, 23 in the 19:00Z power hour and 22 into the 20:00Z close, because a second leg would have to appear inside that window if the current bounce is to fail. Tail then returns to the low band at 19 post-close and decays to a published cycle low of 15 between 04:00Z and 05:00Z as liquidity thins and the easing long-end and contained volatility reduce amplifier alignment. The named overnight checkpoint is the Asian handover: 00:00Z and 01:00Z are held at 19 because Tokyo and Seoul cash trading prices today's 2.79% SOX decline and the Samsung preliminary-results disappointment for the first time, and a chip-led Asian second leg is the stated escalation mechanism. Risk rebuilds modestly through the European session from 16 at 06:00Z to 18 at the 07:00Z cash open, steps to 21 at the 13:00Z hour containing the 13:30Z US open, and reaches a forward peak of 23 at 14:00Z when preliminary Michigan sentiment and its inflation-expectation components print with Brent above $105 and the Fed having already raised rates in September. The final hours ease to 19 into the weekend, where the unresolved Iran conflict is carried as Stress and as a Monday-open gap note rather than as current-path Tail. Stress follows the same shape at a higher level, easing from 68 to 51 overnight and rebuilding to 65 around the Michigan print.
